subject: Usage Insights beta invite + success criteria (route/model cost + exports)
body:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jlee@acmeai.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Usage Insights beta invite + success criteria (route/model cost + exports)

Jordan —

Following up from our enterprise eval thread: we’re preparing a private beta for “Usage Insights” in the Redwood Console focused on granular cost/usage attribution.

What you’ll get in beta (initial scope):
- Cost + usage breakdown by API route + model (e.g., /v1/chat/completions on llama-3.1-70b)
- Drivers surfaced alongside totals: tokens in/out, cache hit/miss, retries, fallbacks, context length distribution, latency-correlated spend
- Exports: CSV download (and a shareable link with RBAC) with totals aligned to billing

We’re putting together a short list of design partners. Would AcmeAI like to be included?

To qualify you for the beta, can you reply with your “success criteria” in plain terms? A few examples we’re hearing:
- “Finance can ingest a weekly CSV to do chargeback by endpoint”
- “Eng lead can see what changed WoW for the top routes”
- “Totals match invoice within an agreed tolerance”

If helpful, I can also send a one-page overview.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference


---

From: Jordan Lee <jlee@acmeai.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta invite + success criteria (route/model cost + exports)

Avery,

Yes — we’d like to be part of the beta.

Success criteria from our side:
1) We can see cost by route/endpoint and model (incl. model version / alias) for our production project.
2) We can export CSV that our finance team can reconcile vs the Redwood invoice.
3) RBAC: only workspace admins (and a small “billing” role) can view cost or export; engineers can see usage but not $.
4) We need to be able to explain drivers (token out spikes, retries, streaming overhead) when spend jumps.

Timeline-wise: we’re trying to have a first pass of internal chargeback reporting by end of March.

Can you send the one-pager?

Jordan
Director of Platform
AcmeAI

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jlee@acmeai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 12:21 PM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta invite + success criteria (route/model cost + exports)

Jordan — super clear, thank you.

Re: timeline: we’re targeting a Console beta in March (rolling enablement via allowlist + feature flag). “End of March” for a usable first pass is consistent with what we’re aiming for.

A couple quick clarifiers so we set expectations correctly:
- Do you need cost grouped by “OpenAI-compatible” endpoints as well (e.g., /v1/responses, /v1/chat/completions), or only Redwood-native routes?
- For model version/alias: do you rely on a stable alias name today (e.g., “acmeai-prod-chat”), or do you want the raw underlying model + version shown too?
- Exports: are you expecting a single CSV for a time range, or programmatic export (API) that you can schedule on your side?

Attaching a draft one-pager (lightweight) — happy to walk through it live.

Attachment: Redwood_Usage_Insights_Beta_Overview.pdf

Avery

From: Jordan Lee <jlee@acmeai.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeai.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 9:08 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta invite + success criteria (route/model cost + exports)

Avery,

Clarifiers:
- We’re using OpenAI-compatible endpoints (mostly /v1/chat/completions + streaming). We’d want the reporting to match what we call from the client libraries.
- For model naming: we use your “aliases” so we need bucketing to avoid duplicates. But we also need the underlying model family/version in the export for analysis.
- Export: ideally both. UI download for ad hoc, plus an API-driven export we can run weekly.

One more: do you plan a “what changed?” view (week over week) that flags token out/cache hit rate changes? Even basic heuristics would help.

Jordan

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jlee@acmeai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeai.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 10:17 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta invite + success criteria (route/model cost + exports)

Jordan — got it.

Looping in Dylan Brooks (Eng lead for Console & Tooling) to confirm a few of the beta details (OpenAI-compat route normalization, export API shape, and the “what changed” heuristics).

Dylan — can you sanity check the below and share what we can commit to for the March beta?
- OpenAI-compatible endpoints appear as canonical routes in insights
- Export supports both UI download + API-driven export job
- Export includes alias + underlying model family/version without duplicate rows
- Basic “what changed?” weekly deltas for top drivers (token out, cache hit rate, retries)

Thanks,
Avery


---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jlee@acmeai.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeai.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 8:46 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta invite + success criteria (route/model cost + exports)

Jordan — Dylan here (I run the Console & Tooling eng team). A few concrete answers.

1) OpenAI-compatible endpoints / route normalization
- Yes: the intent is that whatever you call from client libraries (e.g., /v1/chat/completions, streaming variants) shows up as a stable “canonical route” in the breakdown.
- Caveat for beta: if you have dynamic path segments in any internal proxying, we’ll template/normalize to avoid cardinality explosions. If you can share 3–5 representative routes you rely on, we can validate they bucket correctly.

2) Exports (UI + API)
- Beta includes an async export job (requested from Console, generates a CSV server-side) and a signed download URL.
- The same export job is accessible via API so you can schedule a weekly pull on your side.
- We’ll enforce RBAC and emit audit log events for export creation + download (who/when/what time range).

3) Alias + underlying model family/version
- Agreed requirement. We’re adding “model_family” + “model_version” fields alongside “model_alias” so you can pivot either way.
- We’re also explicitly de-duping alias mapping so you don’t get double rows for aliases pointing to the same underlying model/version.

4) “What changed?” / top drivers
- In beta we’ll have a “Top cost drivers” view and a lightweight “what changed” explanation that flags largest deltas (e.g., token_out up, cache_hit_rate down, retry_rate up, model mix shift).
- We’ll be conservative with copy to avoid misleading conclusions; think: “These 2–3 metrics moved and correlate with spend change,” not a black-box diagnosis.

5) Reconciliation vs invoice
- We’re building reconciliation checks against billing totals. Goal for beta is to match within a defined tolerance; the current target we’re using internally is <= 0.5% drift for a given time window, with clear messaging when data is still “in flight” (late events / aggregation lag).

If it’s useful, I can join a 30-min working session with you + whoever on your finance/FinOps side owns chargeback to walk through the CSV schema and make sure it fits your ingestion.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Engineering Lead, Console & Tooling
Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks. Dylan’s notes line up with what you asked for.

Proposed next steps:
1) You send 3–5 representative endpoints (incl. streaming) + the model aliases you use in prod so we can validate normalization/bucketing.
2) We schedule a 30-min working session (you + a finance/FinOps counterpart; Dylan optional but available) to confirm export columns + reconciliation expectations.
3) We’ll tentatively place AcmeAI on the March beta allowlist pending that validation.

Times that work this week (PT):
- Tue 10:30–11:00
- Wed 1:00–1:30
- Thu 9:00–9:30

If none of those work, send two slots and I’ll adapt.

Avery Johnson
